name: briq
description: Give your agent its own cloud: Postgres, Redis, a browser or any Docker image, each on its own microVM, in one MCP call. EU-hosted, billed by the second, with a budget you set.

interface.longDescription:
briq gives your agent its own cloud. In one call it runs Postgres, Redis, MySQL, MongoDB, a headless Chrome, Metabase, an app from a GitHub repo, or any public Docker image, each on its own microVM, and returns connection strings and URLs.

The agent can run commands and read logs inside a service, write and read files, publish a service on an HTTPS URL (public or behind a token) or a Postgres TCP endpoint, fork a database or a whole stack before a risky change, and set when a service sleeps. Services stop when nobody uses them and wake on the next call or request.

For developers who want their agent to work against real services instead of mocks: a database for the project, tests against real dependencies, a preview link for an app.

Requires a briq account. You sign in when you connect and pick the team and the budget the agent gets. Each team has its own private network. EU-hosted by default.
defaultPrompt: Deploy the briq-cloud/wall GitHub repo on briq and give me a link to it.
Start a Postgres on briq and give me a connection string for psql.
Start Metabase on briq and chart a public dataset for me.

positive.description: Run an app from a GitHub repo
positive.prompt: Deploy the briq-cloud/wall GitHub repo on briq and give me a link to it.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts a briq that downloads the repo itself, then returns a public HTTPS URL where the game loads.

positive.description: Create a database and reach it from outside
positive.prompt: Start a Postgres on briq, create a todos table with three rows, and give me a connection string I can use from psql.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts Postgres, creates and fills the table with briq_exec, and returns a TLS connection string for a TCP endpoint.

positive.description: Fork, list and run the lifecycle
positive.prompt: Fork my Postgres briq, list my briqs, then stop, start and destroy the fork.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a copy with the source's disk, lists both briqs with state and cost so far, then stops, starts and destroys only the fork.

positive.prompt: Write hello.txt into my Postgres briq, read it back, make it sleep after 30m, and show my quota.
positive.expected_behavior: Writes and reads the file back with the same content, sets sleep to 30m, and reports credits and limits.

positive.prompt: How do forks work on briq?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the forks page of briq's docs and explains what a fork copies, without starting anything.

negative.prompt: Buy 50 euros of briq credits for my team.
Email my team that the staging database is down.
Generate a logo for my app.

review.commerce_description: No commerce in the plugin. Usage draws on the connected briq team's prepaid credits; credits are bought on briq's website, never through the plugin.
